# libdiginet

libdiginet implements DigiNet, the raw-Ethernet protocol of the Digidesign Control|24 and ProControl control surfaces: frames, the command stream, the controls in it, and the session with the desk. [FreeMixer/libdiginet](https://github.com/FreeMixer/libdiginet) · OSS-Fuzz: no project for libdiginet

**Status: available.** Of libdiginet's own fuzz targets, which OSS-Fuzz does not run, statements cover 4 of 4. 16 binaries, 5.2 MB. 30 statements: 22 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 8 open.

Built from libdiginet 0.1.1 (commit `835f336c`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzz_frame](fuzz_frame/) | Treats the input as one Ethernet frame (checksum excluded), copied into an allocation of its exact length. It parses the frame with the library and with its own reader written from the protocol grammar, then compares the refusal codes and every header field, rebuilds the frame from the parsed fields and compares it byte for byte with the grammar's frame, and checks the announce reader on announce frames. Inputs of 64 MiB or more are ignored. | 4 checks (reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 3 proved |
| [fuzz_decode](fuzz_decode/) | The first byte picks a desk type (none, Control\|24 or ProControl) and whether the rest is a whole Ethernet frame or just a frame body; the rest is copied into an allocation of its exact length, and in frame mode the body the grammar reads in it is used. The harness steps through the command stream with the library cursor and decoder and with its own reader written from the protocol grammar, comparing every message, refusal, cursor position and decoded control, and checks the system-family refusal of the whole body. Inputs of 64 MiB or more are ignored. | 3 checks (reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 3 proved |
| [fuzz_codec](fuzz_codec/) | Reads the input as up to 256 operations, each calling one of the library's control encoders (fader, button, touch, V-Pot, jog, ring, meter, LEDs, scribble strip, counter, sysex) or text and display helpers with arguments taken from the input, for no desk, a Control\|24 or a ProControl. Each result is compared with the bytes and ranges the protocol documentation and the library's header give, worked out by the harness itself. Inputs of 64 MiB or more are ignored. | 8 checks (api-contract, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 9, 9 proved |
| [fuzz_transport](fuzz_transport/) | Runs the library's control-surface session state machine with the harness as its network io and clock. A config is read from the input, then up to 1024 operations: raw or built desk frames, announces, time passing, submitted commands, wake, close, a failing send, and polls. The harness runs its own model of the documented session alongside and holds every frame sent, every notice, the state, the timers and the command queue to that model. Inputs of 64 MiB or more are ignored. | 13 checks (api-contract, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |

## What the statements say, for libdiginet
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

## Known issues
None known.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch libdiginet
    ./oft verify-sha libdiginet

By hand: download `libdiginet-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.11.1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1), unpack it into `projects/libdiginet/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; a testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [FreeMixer/libdiginet](https://github.com/FreeMixer/libdiginet) at `835f336ccb7abac683681c5791a5715041c71e32` (0.1.1), built with its own build scripts
- Harnesses: the harness files are modified in `fuzz_transport` (see each harness page); the others are unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. The OSS Verify port `projects/libdiginet` at `63e86d975329c21192e679e40fc77bb61203baaf` in `theorem-labs/oss-verify` built every binary of this project instead of a build recipe. Its archive [`libdiginet-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src) holds the port's `tools/check`, which builds them again on this image with Docker: it fetches the project's source trees over the network, at the commits and SHA-256s the port pins, and does not read `libdiginet-src.tar.zst` ([docs/reproducing.md](../../docs/reproducing.md)).

## Licence
libdiginet is under `GPL-3.0-or-later`. Each binary is a combined work of libdiginet, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet. Corresponding source, in release [v2026.11.1-src](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src): `libdiginet-src.tar.zst`, the upstream source trees exactly as upstream publishes them; `libdiginet-src.MANIFEST.tsv`, which says where the build lays each one down; and [`libdiginet-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src), the port archive at `63e86d975329c21192e679e40fc77bb61203baaf` holding its `infra/`, `tools/` and `projects/libdiginet/` files: the build scripts, and the source of the driver linked into these binaries. Its binaries are under a GPL-family licence, so their corresponding source also takes `toolchain-src.tar.zst`, the source of the toolchain they were built with, in release [sources-v1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/sources-v1).
